messages.text: Hello I need help setting up my kbox. My name is Robin L.. I purchased the Kbox. I knew how to set up a miner. This thing thinks it is overheating and it is not but I have no access to heating control? Can you please help.
I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me pull up what I have on your unit before I answer.
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Searched the web · GekkoScience K-Box miner overheating warning temperature set

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed your KBOX over to me.

Quick note first so we are on the same page: the KBOX does have heat control, but it lives in the power mode / tuning section of its web UI (the High 22TH / Medium 16TH / Low 10TH presets), not as a fan slider. 
It runs the three presets High (22TH), Medium (16TH) and Low (10TH)
, and 
if either fan stops, hashing stops, with a software limit on ASIC temperature and a hardware limit on the main voltage regulator behind it
. So an "overheat" state is usually either a real temp reading, a stalled fan reading, or a sensor the firmware is not reading right.

One thing at a time. Can you give me two facts:

1. The exact wording of the overheat message and where you see it (front screen, or the web UI dashboard), and the temperature numbers it is showing you right now.
2. The firmware version shown in the KBOX web UI (usually under System or Settings).

A screenshot of that dashboard page is even better if you can grab one. I will not guess at the message from memory, I want to read it against your exact firmware.
Ok

Got the screenshot, thanks. I can see it: this is the Device & Maintenance panel of the KBOX web UI (API key section above, Check for updates, changelog, rollback, Restart, then the red Danger Zone with Shutdown and Factory Reset, Advanced below, footer credits to sidehack / GekkoScience for hardware and I Am GPIO / thesolomining.co for software). No temperature or version is shown on this part of the page.

So two things from here, in order:

1. Press "Check for updates". Firmware first, always: a bad or over-sensitive temp reading is the kind of thing that gets fixed in a release. Tell me what version it reports you are on and whether it offers a newer one. Do not touch Factory Reset or Shutdown yet.

2. Then scroll to the main dashboard / home page of the UI and send me a screenshot of that, the part with the hashrate and the temperature readings. That is where I will see what the unit actually thinks it is measuring (ASIC temp vs voltage regulator temp vs a fan reading at zero).

One more thing for context while you do that: what is the unit doing right now, is it still hashing at reduced speed, or has it stopped hashing entirely?
I did the restart it did not work

Understood, a restart alone rarely clears this one.

Next single step: in that same Device & Maintenance panel, press "Check for updates" and tell me what it says, specifically the version number you are on now and whether it offers a newer one. If it offers one, run it and let the box come back up on its own (it can take a few minutes, do not pull power during an update).

While that runs, two quick facts I still need:

1. Is the unit hashing at all right now, or stopped?
2. Can you hear the fans spinning?

That second one matters: the KBOX stops hashing on purpose if either fan reading drops to zero, and that stop can read as an overheat condition even when the box is cold. If one fan is dead or its tachometer is not reporting, the box behaves exactly as you describe.
Ok 1sec
No rush, take your time. I am here.
No updates needed it said

Good, so firmware is current and we can rule that out.

Next step, the one that will tell us what the box is actually measuring: scroll up to the main dashboard page of the web UI and send me a screenshot of it, the section with the hashrate, the temperatures and the fan speeds.

And the two answers I asked for, if you have them:

1. Is it hashing right now, or stopped?
2. Can you hear both fans running?

Once I see those readings I can tell you whether this is a sensor reporting nonsense, a fan the firmware cannot read, or a genuine thermal condition.
The machine is not hot

I believe you, and that fits: the box can report an overheat state while the metal is cold. That is why I want the numbers rather than the feel.

One thing only, then: go back to the top of that same web page (the dashboard / home view with the hashrate) and take a photo of it the same way you did the last one. I need to see the temperature and fan readings the firmware is showing.

If a reading sits at 0 or at some absurd number, that is a sensor or a fan tachometer, not real heat, and it is fixable. If the ASIC temp is genuinely high while the case is cold, that points somewhere else entirely.
Front & sides & top are room temperature

That tells me something useful: a KBOX that is actually hashing gets warm everywhere, so room temperature on all surfaces means it is almost certainly not hashing at all, it has cut out and is sitting there reporting overheat.

So the one question that splits this in two, and it is a listen-and-feel check, no UI needed:

With the unit powered on, can you hear the fans, and do you feel air moving at the vents? Yes or no is enough.

- Fans dead or one dead: that is the fan-stop cutoff. The K. stops hashing if either fan stops, so it never gets hot, and the fault surfaces as an overheat state.
- Fans both spinning fine: then the firmware is reading a temperature sensor wrong, and the dashboard numbers will show it.

Either way I will still want that dashboard photo when you can, but answer the fan question first.
Ok
Take your time, I am waiting on the fan answer: can you hear them spinning and feel air at the vents, yes or no.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that confirms the firmware: you are on v1.20.0, the latest main, so firmware is ruled out.

One housekeeping note first: that screenshot shows your API key in full. It is like a password. Press "Regenerate key" on that panel when you get a moment, it instantly revokes the one in the photo. Nothing else needed.

Now, this is still the Security / API / Maintenance part of the page. What I need is the very top of the dashboard, the part with the hashrate, the temperatures and the fan speeds. Scroll all the way up and photograph that.

And still open, the quickest check of all: with the box powered on, can you hear the fans spinning and feel air at the vents?
I have 5 pictures

Thanks, I can read that one: the Mining tab, pool set to stratum+tcp://stratum.kano.is:3333, user is a BTC address, password x, dual mining off. That part is fine and not related to the heat issue.

Go ahead and send all 5, one after the other. The two I most need are:

1. The top of the dashboard, with the hashrate, temperature and fan readings.
2. The S. tab (the row of tabs you are on now: Mining, Network, Display, System, Help). That is where the power mode and tuning controls live, which is the "heat control" you said you had no access to.

Send what you have and I will read each one.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Read it: Network tab, radio on, WiFi credentials stored but not yet connected, Ethernet connected, and it is joining LUNNYHOME now. Networking is fine, the box is reachable over Ethernet.

Keep them coming. The S. tab and the dashboard top are the two I need.
